newsitem.title: USA: Stock market snaps losing streak.
newsitem.headline: Stock market snaps losing streak.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks rose Monday, snapping a three-session losing streak that followed Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's remarks last Wednesday about high stock prices and possibly higher interest rates.
The Dow Jones industrial average jumped 41.18 points to 6,918.92 after losing more than 160 points the last three sessions.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,287 to 1,211 on moderate volume of 432.6 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

But Greenspan's remarks still rippled through the bond market, where the 30-year Treasury fell 12/32, or $3.75 on a $1,000 bond, raising its yield to 6.83 percent from 6.80 percent on Friday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.

Investors were also greeted with a rude surprise Monday when AT&T Corp. outlined plans to enter new local telephone and wireless markets that will require massive spending, eating into earnings. AT&T fell 3-1/8 to 36-3/4.
The weak bond market, coupled with AT&T's decline, made the stock market's moderate gains appear all the more impressive, analysts said.
"You had two major negatives today and the market was still able to basically reverse course," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.

When buyers did emerge, they descended on the technology stocks that led the market to record highs in mid-February and lately have led it back down. Intel Corp. rose four to 145-7/8, International Business Machines Corp. was up 1-1/2 to 145-1/4 and Microsoft Corp. rose two to 99-1/2.
Analysts called the rebound encouraging but stopped short of predicting an end to the market's recent weakness.
"It's going to be a while before these stocks regain their luster," said Joseph Barthel, chief investment strategist at Fahnestock & Co.

Analysts noted that Greenspan's scheduled appearance before the House Banking Committee on Wednesday and a key monthly employment report due on Friday would likely preclude any meaningful rise in stocks in the meantime.
But with the broad market following tech stocks higher and shrugging off the AT&T surprise, analysts said it was clear that at least one major change had occurred on Wall Street.
"I'm not certain AT&T is viewed as a bellwether anymore," Barthel said. "Now we look to companies like Intel and Microsoft."

Among individual issues, Conrail Inc. surged 7-1/8 to 111-5/8 as expectation mounted that a four-month takeover battle for control of the railroad was nearing an end. Conrail said its board was meeting on Monday to discuss the company's options. Analysts predicted Conrail's assets would be divided between rival bidders CSX Corp. amd Norfolk Southern Corp.
CSX jumped 2-7/8 to 49 and Norfolk Southern rose 2-3/4 to 93-7/8.
BHC Financial Inc. soared 11-7/8 to 31-7/8 after the company agreed to be acquired by Fiserv Inc. Fiserv climbed 3-7/8 to 36-5/8.

COR Therapeutics Inc. slid 2-15/16 to 9-3/8 after a Food and Drug Administration advisory panel recommended against approving intrifiban, a rattlesnake venom derivative the company hoped to market for treating some heart conditions.
The Nasdaq composite index rose 2.18 points 1,311.18.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 4.49 points to 795.31. The American Stock Exchange index edged up 0.58 to 594.82.
The NYSE composite index of all listed common stocks rose 1.83 to 417.34. The average share was up 19 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,591.522, up 32.105 or 0.42 percent.
